conclusion: Three alternating, unmodified upstream loopback pairs completed on logical CPUs 0,2,4,6 with Tokio/GOMAXPROCS=4. Rust Criterion 64-byte sample means were 45.961–47.990 us versus upstream Go aggregate means 40.173–41.621 us; 2 MiB requests with 1-byte acknowledgements were 15.523–17.054 ms for Rust and 37.703–74.245 ms for Go. These are separate estimators, not speed-ratio claims. Native aggregate outputs neither confirm nor rule out individual 10–23 ms stalls. The preliminary adapter used max_connections=10 and no LTO; the final adapter selects max_connections=1 and matching thin-LTO release settings, but neither change proves the cause of its elevated preliminary means.
limitations: Criterion sample mean/slope and Go testing aggregate ns/op are distinct estimators; no cross-estimator ratios or individual-message percentiles are inferred.

Native Criterion warms each connection for one second and measures long steady-state batches; our custom adapter uses a fresh connection per size, one readiness echo, and only 100 or 10 measured echoes.
Upstream cases are 64-byte full echo and 2 MiB request/1-byte acknowledgement, not the main report's 32/512/4096/65536-byte full echoes.
Upstream Go pins lunar 6124f52657d4; the main harness pins lunar 87a6b7e53799.
Upstream sources and default optimized bench profile were preserved; the final custom adapter's thin-LTO profile is not applied to this diagnostic run.
Go testing on this Windows toolchain already uses QueryPerformanceCounter/Frequency; no published benchmark clock patch or substituted custom harness was used.
Three alternating rounds on a shared workstation do not reproduce historical published hardware/toolchains or validate exact reported multipliers.
Preliminary main-report values are preserved as historical diagnostics; final adapter connection-limit and release-profile alignment does not establish causality for its tails.
Raw Rust stdout has Windows non-ASCII glyph decoding artifacts; numeric table values use preserved Criterion JSON. Exact absolute commands and working directories are recorded in raw commands.json.
